translationRepairs: Duan Rong, styled Zimao, was a native of Gugang in Wuwei.
Duan Rong, styled Zimao, was a native of Guzang in Wuwei.
姑臧 is the Wuwei seat Guzang; Gugang is a false romanization of the place-name in 姑臧武威人也.
Duan Rong, styled Zimao, was a native of Gugang in Wuwei.
Duan Rong, styled Zimao, was a native of Guzang in Wuwei.
Literal likewise misreads 姑臧 as Gugang; Guzang restores the correct place-name.
When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, for merit Duan Rong was enfeoffed marquis of Gugang County with a fief of eight hundred households.
When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, for merit Duan Rong was enfeoffed marquis of Guzang County with a fief of eight hundred households.
封姑臧縣侯 enfeoffs him Marquis of Guzang County; Gugang County invents a wrong toponym.
When the Grand Ancestor entered Luoyang, for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Gugang County with a fief of eight hundred households.
When the Grand Ancestor entered Luoyang, for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Guzang County with a fief of eight hundred households.
Literal repeats Gugang for 姑臧縣侯; Guzang County matches the Chinese title.
In the first year of Yuanxiang, he was granted three imperators' protocol.
In the first year of Yuanxiang, he was granted Equal to the Three Dukes.
授儀同三司 is the rank Equal to the Three Dukes, not “three imperators’ protocol”; drop the leftover “protocol” wording while keeping the correct office name.
In the first year of Yuanxiang, he was granted three imperators' protocol.
In the first year of Yuanxiang, he was granted Equal to the Three Dukes.
Literal has the same 儀同三司 garble; grant Equal to the Three Dukes without retaining “protocol”.
They attacked Liu Yan at Ye.
They attacked Liu Dan at Ye.
劉誕 romanizes as Liu Dan; Yan misreads 誕 and invents the wrong given name.
They attacked Liu Yan at Ye.
They attacked Liu Dan at Ye.
Literal likewise has Liu Yan for 劉誕; Liu Dan is the accurate personal name.
Later, by grace his father Duan Rong was given the title marquis of Gugang County; Shao petitioned to yield his barony of Xialuo County to his younger half-brother Ning'an.
Later, by grace his father Duan Rong was given the title marquis of Guzang County; Shao petitioned to yield his barony of Xialuo County to his younger half-brother Ning'an.
父榮姑臧縣侯 again names Guzang County; Gugang is the same false romanization as earlier.
Later, by grace his father Rong was given the title Marquis of Gugang County; Shao petitioned to yield his barony of Xialuo County to his younger half-brother Ning'an.
Later, by grace his father Rong was given the title Marquis of Guzang County; Shao petitioned to yield his barony of Xialuo County to his younger half-brother Ning'an.
Literal Marquis of Gugang County misreads 姑臧縣侯; Guzang County is correct.
He left acting three imperators' Jing Xianjun, Yao Nazong, and others to besiege and hold Suyu; he himself led several thousand infantry and cavalry by forced march toward Jing Province.
He left Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes Jing Xianjun, Yao Nazong, and others to besiege and hold Suyu; he himself led several thousand infantry and cavalry by forced march toward Jing Province.
儀同 before 敬顯儁 is the Yitong rank (Equal to the Three Dukes), not “acting three imperators”.
He left Acting Three Imperators' Jing Xianjun, Yao Nazong, and others to besiege and hold Suyu; he himself led several thousand infantry and cavalry by forced march toward Jing Province.
He left Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes Jing Xianjun, Yao Nazong, and others to besiege and hold Suyu; he himself led several thousand infantry and cavalry by forced march toward Jing Province.
Literal “Acting Three Imperators” garble of 儀同; Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes restores the office title.

In the twelfth month, Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou dispatched generals leading Qiang and tribal forces together with the Turks in a combined host pressing Jinyang; Gao Yan hurried from Ye by forced march to the rescue.

In the twelfth month, Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou dispatched generals leading Qiang and tribal forces together with the Turks in a combined host pressing Jinyang; Emperor Wucheng hurried from Ye by forced march to the rescue.
世祖自鄴…赴救 is Emperor Wucheng (temple name Shizu), not Gao Yan; the idiomatic misidentifies the Qi ruler.
Events were sudden; troops and horses were not yet arrayed. Seeing this, the Later Lord also wished to withdraw eastward.
Events were sudden; troops and horses were not yet arrayed. Seeing this, the Shizu Emperor also wished to withdraw eastward.
世祖見如此 is Shizu/Emperor Wucheng; “Later Lord” names a different Northern Qi emperor (後主).
They will be weary and we rested — defeat is certain."
They will be weary and we rested — defeating them is certain."
破之必矣 means breaking them (the enemy) is certain; “defeat is certain” reverses who is defeated.
The Later Lord commended his merit, separately enfeoffed him Duke of Wude Commandery in Huai Province, and advanced him to Grand Preceptor.
The Shizu Emperor commended his merit, separately enfeoffed him Duke of Wude Commandery in Huai Province, and advanced him to Grand Preceptor.
世祖嘉其功 is Shizu/Emperor Wucheng, not the Later Lord.
The Later Lord sent Attendant of the Yellow Gate Xu Shirong by fast relay with the Zhou letter to consult Shao.
The Shizu Emperor sent Attendant of the Yellow Gate Xu Shirong by fast relay with the Zhou letter to consult Shao.
世祖遣黃門…问韶 again names Shizu; Later Lord is the wrong emperor.
The Later Lord summoned Shao and said, "I wish to send you to the siege at Luoyang — but the Turks are here and must still be held in check. What do you think?"
The Shizu Emperor summoned Shao and said, "I wish to send you to the siege at Luoyang — but the Turks are here and must still be held in check. What do you think?"
世祖召謂曰 continues Shizu’s speech; Later Lord is a false identification.
The Later Lord said, "My mind is the same."
The Shizu Emperor said, "My mind is the same."
世祖曰：「朕意亦爾」 is Shizu speaking; Later Lord does not appear in the Chinese.

The imperial carriage visited Luoyang and personally encouraged the soldiers. At Heyin a great feast of wine was set out; merits were assessed and rewards given — Shao was made grand preceptor and enfeoffed duke of Lingwu County.

The imperial carriage visited Luoyang and personally encouraged the soldiers. At Heyin a great feast of wine was set out; merits were assessed and rewards given — Shao was made grand steward and enfeoffed duke of Lingwu County.
除太宰 appoints Grand Steward (太宰), not Grand Preceptor (太師).

The imperial carriage visited Luoyang and personally encouraged the soldiers; at Heyin a great feast of wine was set out, merits were assessed and rewards given — Shao was made Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed Duke of Lingwu County.

The imperial carriage visited Luoyang and personally encouraged the soldiers; at Heyin a great feast of wine was set out, merits were assessed and rewards given — Shao was made Grand Steward and enfeoffed Duke of Lingwu County.
Literal likewise confuses 太宰 with Grand Preceptor; Grand Steward matches the Chinese office.
Better to build another fortress to block their route, break Fucheng, and join forces against Dingyang — that is the longer plan."
Better to build another fortress to block their route, break Qincheng, and join forces against Dingyang — that is the longer plan."
破服秦 continues the place 服秦(城); Fucheng is a mistranslation, and Qincheng aligns with that toponym.
Better to build another fortress to block their route, break Fucheng, and join forces against Dingyang — that is the longer plan."
Better to build another fortress to block their route, break Qincheng, and join forces against Dingyang — that is the longer plan."
Literal Fucheng likewise misreads 破服秦; Qincheng restores the place named in the Chinese.
At the end of the Wuding era he entered service as an army aide in the Secretariat.
At the end of the Wei Wuding era he began his career as an army aide to the Minister over the Masses (Situ).
魏武定末，起家司徒參軍事 begins under the Situ (Minister over the Masses), not the Secretariat, and the idiomatic had dropped 魏.
At the end of the Wei Wuding era, he began his career as an army aide in the Secretariat.
At the end of the Wei Wuding era, he began his career as an army aide to the Minister over the Masses (Situ).
Literal keeps Wei but mistranslates 司徒 as Secretariat; Situ/Minister over the Masses is correct.
